compiled_state.title: As an agent operator, the remediation loop classifies and normalizes Tier 2, 3, and 4 CI failures
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Extend lib/ci-findings-normalize.sh with Tier 2 (test), Tier 3 (lint), and Tier 4 (other/unknown) schemas; add gh run view log parsing fallback when artifacts are absent; implement ARTIFACT_MISSING detection; implement priority-order dispatch loop (Tier 1 → 2 → 3 → 4).

**Why**: Completes the 4-tier failure classification required by SC1 and enables the normalizer to handle any CI failure type, not just llm-review.

**Scope**:
- IN: Tier 2/3/4 normalizer functions in lib/ci-findings-normalize.sh; gh run view log parsing fallback (pytest/jest output, ruff/eslint output); ARTIFACT_MISSING detection path; priority-order processing loop (1→2→3→4); each tier re-polls CI before advancing to next tier
- OUT: Bounding counters (→S4); escalation payload beyond ARTIFACT_MISSING (→S4)

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, test failures (Tier 2), lint failures (Tier 3), and other/unknown failures (Tier 4) are classified and normalized into the review-fix-dispatch findings format
  ← Satisfies: "SC1: The remediation loop classifies CI check failures into four tiers"
- When this story is complete, if no CI artifacts are uploaded for a tier, the normalizer falls back to gh run view log parsing; if that also produces no parseable output, ARTIFACT_MISSING is returned for that tier
  ← Satisfies: "SC4: stop_reason enum includes ARTIFACT_MISSING"
- When this story is complete, tiers are processed in priority order (1→2→3→4); each tier's fixes are pushed and CI is re-polled before the loop advances to the next failing tier
  ← Satisfies: "SC1: dispatches the appropriate fix strategy per tier"
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified normalizer functions in lib/ci-findings-normalize.sh

## Considerations

- [Testing] Log parsing fallback requires mock CI log output fixtures for pytest, jest, ruff, eslint formats
- [Reliability] gh run view may timeout for large CI logs — consider timeout handling and truncation
- [Security] gh run view log-parsing path reads raw CI logs which may contain secrets (tokens echoed by failing tests, API keys in environment dumps) — apply the same redaction/no-raw-log policy as Tier 1 artifact handling
- [Maintainability] Normalizer schema must match review-fix-dispatch's expected findings format; reuse the schema-conformance test fixture established in S1

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
